text: {"distance_m": 5, "reasoning_short": "A small, low-contrast spot's visibility depends on contrast times area, not on 20/20 acuity alone. From approximate recall of Blackwell-type threshold data for indoor lighting, a 15% contrast disk needs roughly 2–3 arcmin to be detected. A 4 mm spot subtends 3 arcmin at about 4.6 m and 2.2 arcmin at about 6 m, so the limit is roughly 5 m."}
